body: a dune-hauler mecha-camel, full clean side-profile reference view, standing on all four legs facing left, legs clearly separated and fully visible, a single hump housing a cargo/water tank with a small brass gauge window showing the level inside, an empty rider saddle mounted just ahead of the hump (no rider), a long armored neck and calm-eyed head. Sun-baked adobe clay #c9764f body plating, sun-brass #e8c45c trim and joint fittings (the SAME gold family as the Grand Forge's own metalwork -- this mount should look like it rolled straight out of that forge), deep shadow-violet #3a2a4a in the recessed panel gaps and undercarriage shadow. TURTLE'S NOTE: wide splayed feet built for sand, not hooves -- these should read as pressure-distributing plates, functional desert engineering, and the whole silhouette should feel unhurried and durable, built to cross real distance between the Grand Forge and the Air Pad, not built for speed. Cinematic occult-almanac quality render, harsh desert midday sun with hard-edged shadow, plain flat sand-grey background so the silhouette reads clearly, full body visible head to tail, no text, no logos, no rider, no watermark
